## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components combined with a fused scatter can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured N exceed the L1d spill at N≈949. The L2 spill at N≈60787 falls between N=10000 and N=100000. At q=0.01, cost FALLS across this boundary — 8.82 ns/p at N=10000 → 7.848 at N=100000 → 7.4 at N=10000000 — with no knee at the L2→DRAM transition. Overhead amortization dominates small N; the curve flattens by N=100000. Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: at q=0.5 the floor sits at ~12.9 ns/p but stays flat across all N, confirming cache capacity is not binding.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 9.32 GB/s at N=10000000, q=0.01 — 31% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. The algo is compute/overhead-bound: bandwidth rises modestly with N (7.82→9.32) from amortization, not cache effects, and never transitions toward bandwidth-bound. Death rate contracts bandwidth monotonically: 9.32→8.0→6.66→5.35 GB/s at q=0.01/0.1/0.25/0.5. Branch_flush grows from 5.9% to 21.3%, consuming cycles that would otherwise go to compute.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across components of one particle, not across particles. `fmul.4s v7, v18, v3` and `fadd.4s v7, v16, v7` operate on four floats within one particle; `ext.16b v18, v16, v17, #0xc` and `mov.s v18[3], v7[0]` rearrange lanes. `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x10]` is an indexed single-lane gather. Per-particle stride is 0x44 (68 bytes), so `ldur q16` loads only one particle's block — never contiguous particles. The fused scatter uses byte-granular `strb` stores (`strb w16, [x15]`, `[x15, #0x1]`, `[x15, #0x2]`) with `csel` clamping — byte writes that cannot stream. Component-wise vec on stride-0x44 explains the low bandwidth; the scatter's byte stores cap it at 31%.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak 9.32 GB/s at N=10000000, q=0.01 is only 31% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. The fused scatter's byte-granular `strb` writes and component-wise-only vectorization (stride 0x44, no cross-particle contiguous loads) prevent streaming regardless of N. Branch_flush rises from 5.9% to 21.3% by q=0.5, dropping bandwidth to 5.35 GB/s. The hypothesis fails even at the lowest churn measured.
